_readme: Riffs, leads, and a recommended amp tone for each backing track in tracks.json, keyed by track id. Original phrases, CC0. tab is one token per note: string (e B G D A E, high e lowercase), fret, optional techniques (hN hammer, pN pull-off, bN bend to fret N, sN or /N slide to fret N, ~ vibrato), duration (w h. h q. q e. e s; default q). Double-stops: B5+G7e. r plus a duration is a rest. | marks a bar line and must match the track's bars. tone.slot is a factory preset; overrides replace its delay, feedback, mix, drive, or cabinet IR.

tone.name: Cold Shot
tone.why: Texas blues: a Deluxe on the vibrato channel at the edge of breakup, through the LX TDR Marshall 1 cab IR. The delay is cut to an eighth-note triplet at 96 BPM so it slaps inside the shuffle instead of smearing it.

phrases.title: Shuffle boogie riff
phrases.tip: Root, flat 3, 4 on the root's string, one shape per chord. Palm-mute lightly and swing the eighths.

phrases.title: Texas shuffle solo
phrases.tip: Box 1 at the 5th fret: pick the first note in each pair, then hammer or pull the rest. The G8b10 bend is the flat 5 crying up toward the 5th — support with three fingers behind the bend.

techniqueTips.text: Bars 1–2: B5h8 and G5h7 — one pick, two notes. Keep the hammer finger low so it snaps the string.
Bar 3: G8b10 over Am7 — bend to the pitch of fret 10 (B). Release on the rest so the shuffle pocket stays open.
Bar 5: B5+G7e over Dm7 — both notes are in the scale; strum lightly with the pick edge.
Bar 9: e8p5p8 — trill flavor on the turnaround; pull toward the floor.
Bar 11: B5s8 — slide into the root for the last Am7 bar before the V.
Bar 12: hold G7~h on Em7 — slow wrist vibrato on the flat 7 (D).

tone.name: Brit 2204
tone.why: A JCM800-style crunch through the LX TDR Marshall 2 cab IR: tight enough for eighth-note pedal tones, with a quiet eighth-note delay at 120 BPM.

phrases.title: Eighth-note pedal riff
phrases.tip: Drive the root in straight eighths and walk up into the next chord on the last two. Downpicks only.

tone.name: Essex A30
tone.why: AC30 chime for open-chord pop, through the LX TDR Marshall 2 cab IR. A dotted-eighth delay at 108 BPM (417 ms) turns the arpeggios into a shimmer.

phrases.title: Open-chord arpeggios
phrases.tip: Hold each chord shape and pick one string at a time so the notes ring over each other.

phrases.title: Pop hook with slides
phrases.tip: Open-position G major: slides connect chord tones across the I–V–vi–IV. Let dotted-eighth delay carry notes you sustain.

techniqueTips.text: Bar 1: G0/G2 — slide from open G to A on the G string for a vocal pickup into the G chord.
Bar 2: e0h2 over D — hammer the 2nd fret (F#) without a second pick; that's the major 3rd of D.
Bar 3: B3b5 over Em — quarter-step feel bend toward C; stay short so you land on B for the chord.
Bar 4: B1+G0q over C — 3rd and root of C; pick both strings with one stroke.
Bar 6: B3p0 — pull off to open B string for a bell-like decay on D.
Bar 8: G0~h — slow vibrato on the root ending the form.

tone.name: Funky Meercat
tone.why: A clean Deluxe with the treble a little up, through the LX TDR Marshall 1 cab IR. Funk wants it dry, so the delay is a barely-there sixteenth (147 ms at 102 BPM).

phrases.title: Sixteenth-note funk line
phrases.tip: Keep your picking hand moving in sixteenths even on the rests. Short, choked notes: lift the fretting finger right after each one.

phrases.title: Dorian call and response
phrases.tip: Sixteenth-grid funk: stay muted between hits. On G7 bars, B natural is the Dorian color — hammer and slide into it, never bend it sharp.

techniqueTips.text: Bar 1: G5h7 — pick once, then hammer to the 7th fret on the same string.
Bar 3: B6+G7e on G7 — 3rd and flat 7 together; short and percussive.
Bar 5: e5s7 — slide up into the Dorian 6th over Dm7.
Bar 6: B8p6p5 — descending answer on the B string; keep the picking hand in sixteenths.
Bar 7: G7b9 over G7 — bend to the 9th fret pitch (A); release before the next stab.
Bar 8: e7~q — one sustained target with wrist vibrato to fill the last G7 bar.

tone.name: Open Chordus PH
tone.why: Clean and wide through the Mesa Mark IIC+ cab IR. A dotted-eighth delay at 126 BPM (357 ms) locks to the four-on-the-floor.

phrases.title: Offbeat octave stabs
phrases.tip: Play only the 'and' of each beat, root then octave. Mute the string between stabs so it pumps with the kick.

tone.name: Another Thing
tone.why: A 2204-style stack through the LX TDR Marshall 2 cab IR, hot enough for open-E chugs. The delay is a short eighth at 136 BPM (221 ms), just enough to thicken leads.

phrases.title: Open-E chug riff
phrases.tip: Palm-mute the open E and lift the mute for the F# and D. The D is the flat 7 that makes this Mixolydian.

phrases.tip: G# (B string 9th fret) is the major 3rd. Lean on it over E, then slide to the A shape for the A bars.

tone.name: MK IV lead 2
tone.why: A Mesa Mark IV lead through the Mesa Mark IIC+ cab IR: smooth, singing sustain for neoclassical lines. Dotted-eighth delay at 72 BPM (625 ms).

tone.why: The acoustic preset with no amp model, swapped onto the slope-shoulder dreadnought IR for a flatpicker's boom. A faint eighth-note slap at 184 BPM (163 ms) and almost no mix.

tone.name: Dreamy Lead
tone.why: A clean Archetype with a long dotted-eighth delay at 64 BPM (703 ms) and high feedback, through the Mesa Mark IIC+ cab IR: notes bloom into the pad.

phrases.tip: One note per beat, letting every string ring. G# over E (G string 1st fret) is the Lydian color.
